title: Cowan Recreation Centre opening day celebration brings more than 6000 community members together
content: Kitchener, ON - Thousands of visitors joined City Council, government representatives, community partners and business leaders today in commemoration of the grand opening of the Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park, marking a new era of recreation, wellness and connection in Kitchener.
The day-long celebration welcomed families, neighbours and community members of all ages to explore the City's newest and most accessible facility.

“Together with the outgoing Kitchener City Council, I was thrilled today to join our Kitchener residents and others to see the Cowan Recreation Centre officially come to life,” said Mayor Berry Vrbanovic. “As I have witnessed the facility in recent weeks during its soft opening, and again today, what has stood out to me was how naturally people seemed to have a true sense of belonging in all its many spaces. Kids are making new friends while they swim in the pool, neighbours will meet as they use the walking track, and local athletes are exploring new possibilities for their sport. It's clear that the Cowan Recreation Centre will have an immeasurable impact because our community will shape what happens here every day.”

Following today’s ribbon-cutting ceremony, residents spent the day exploring the Cowan Recreation Centre through a range of free activities and programs. Visitors toured the facility, connected with community organizations and sport groups, participated in family activities and recreation programs, and made use of amenities including the aquatics centre, walking track and FIFA-sized indoor turf. More than 6,000 visitors participated in activities throughout the day, including approximately 1,200 joining free public swims, 200 residents taking part in recreation programs and more than 3,000 enjoying refreshments with their visit onsite. Programming continued into the evening with organized recreation sports, fitness classes and drop-in opportunities for children, teens and adults.

“Today showed what it means to build a recreation centre for everyone,” said Michael May, Deputy Chief Administrative Officer for the City of Kitchener. “The Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park is the most accessible facility the City has ever built, and today we welcomed residents of all ages and abilities to take part wide variety of activities, connect with their neighbours and enjoy time with friends.”

The grand opening celebration is just the beginning of 9-days of free activities designed to help residents discover everything the Cowan Recreation Centre has to offer. Visitors are encouraged to check out the schedule and register online before arriving .

Starting on Sunday, November 15, and continuing throughout the week, residents can experience the facility firsthand through free recreational programming designed to meet a range of skills and abilities, including fitness and wellness classes, aquatics programs, recreation sports, active aging opportunities, youth activities and facility tours. Pre-registration through ActiveNet is required for most activities . Drop-in activities will be available on Sunday, November 15.

The celebration concludes with a showcase of local sport organizations, giving residents an opportunity to watch demonstrations, meet local community partners and discover pathways to lifelong participation in sport, recreation and active living.
To learn more about programming and events, visit Kitchener.ca/RBJSchlegelPark .

title: A place to connect, compete and belong: Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park officially opens doors to the community
content: Kitchener, ON - Today, the City of Kitchener officially opened the new Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park, celebrating a landmark investment in community building through recreation and sport.
Guided by the vision of helping residents connect, compete and belong, the Cowan Recreation Centre was built to support both everyday recreation and meaningful community experiences.

Designed to be the most accessible facility the City has ever created, and located in one of Kitchener's fastest-growing communities, the Cowan Recreation Centre is expected to welcome more than 500,000 visits annually. The centre provides opportunities for residents of all ages and abilities through sport, recreation and community activities, establishing RBJ Schlegel Park as a premier, year-round recreation destination for Kitchener and the surrounding region.

"The Cowan Recreation Centre is a generational investment in our community that will serve our residents for decades to come," said City of Kitchener Mayor Berry Vrbanovic. " The true value of this facility won't be measured by its size or amenities, but by the experiences that happen within it.  It will be a place where people come together, support one another, celebrate achievements, and find community and belonging. Those everyday moments are where this centre will make its indelible mark on the lives of people of all ages in our city."

The opening ceremony reflected the partnerships that helped bring the project to life and included remarks from Mayor Berry Vrbanovic; Member of Parliament Kitchener-Conestoga Tim Louis; Jess Dixon, Member of Provincial Parliament for Kitchener South–Hespeler and Parliamentary Assistant to the Minister of Sport; Michael May, Deputy Chief Administrative Officer, City of Kitchener; Indigenous community leader Myeengun Henry, who led the opening smudging ceremony; and Olympic boxer Mandy Bujold, who spoke on behalf of local athletes. Representatives from the City’s Integrated Project Delivery (IPD) team, Atiaan Stander from Multiplex and Bill Lett from Unity, and community funding partners Jamie Schlegel and Maureen Cowan also participated in the celebration.

Grand opening celebrations continue throughout the week for Kitchener residents. From November 14 to 22, residents of all ages are invited to explore the Cowan Recreation Centre at their own pace – and at no charge. Visitors are encouraged to pre-register to take part in activities such as free public swims, try new programs and facility amenities, and watch local athletes in action.

While built to primarily serve Kitchener residents, the Cowan Recreation Centre is also an investment in Kitchener's economic future, as the centre is expected to generate significant economic benefits both during and after construction.

The Cowan Recreation Centre is also home to Canada's first multi-sport glass floor. Located in the facility's quad gymnasium, the innovative surface uses LED technology to display digital sport lines that can be reconfigured at the touch of a button. Designed to enhance accessibility, improve participant experience and reduce long-term maintenance costs, the floor allows the centre to offer activities ranging from basketball and volleyball, to emerging sports like futsal, as well as offering opportunities for wheelchair sports and adaptive recreation programming.

The centre is expected to attract major tournaments and sporting events, bringing athletes, coaches, officials and families from outside the community, bolstering Kitchener's tourism sector and generating spending at local hotels, restaurants, retailers and other businesses.

Designed to support the City of Kitchener's climate and sustainability goals, the Cowan Recreation Centre is the City’s first net-zero carbon building, and also one of the most sustainable recreation facilities in Canada. The facility incorporates industry-leading energy efficiency measures and net-zero design principles that will significantly reduce greenhouse gas emissions while lowering long-term operating costs.

Through investments in sustainable building systems and energy-efficient technologies, the facility demonstrates how major community infrastructure can support both environmental stewardship and exceptional recreation experiences for residents.

“Cowan Recreation Centre represents an investment in both our community and our future,” said Michael May, Deputy Chief Administrative Officer. “Completed on time and on budget, this facility will provide lasting value for residents and become a cornerstone of community life, contributing to the vibrancy, vitality and sense of belonging that make Kitchener such a great place to live.”
The Cowan Recreation Centre was made possible through significant investments from all levels of government, including:
$11.7 million in funding from the Government of Canada
$9.788 million federal portion of the Investing in Canada Infrastructure Program (ICIP)
$2 million Green and Inclusive Community Buildings (GICB) program
$18.1 million in funding from the Government of Ontario
$8.156 million through Ontario’s portion of the ICIP
$10 million through Ontario’s Community Sport and Recreation Infrastructure Fund (CSRIF), specifically supporting the quad gymnasium.

The project was further strengthened by the generous donations of local community partners, including The Schlegel family and The Cowan Foundation, whose support has given Kitchener residents a place to gather and play for decades to come.
To discover even more grand opening week festivities or learn about the Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park visit rbjschlegelpark.ca .
ADDITIONAL QUOTES

“The Cowan Recreation Centre is one of the most substantial pieces of infrastructure to open in Kitchener. As one of the biggest projects undertaken in our city’s history, this sports hub will provide space to compete, practice, and gather for generations to come. The Government of Canada’s support for the Cowan Recreation Centre and other critical infrastructure across the country is building Canada strong.” - Tim Louis, Member of Parliament for Kitchener-Conestoga.

"Ontario is proud to invest in community infrastructure that keeps people healthy, our community connected and our local economy strong. With more than $18 million in provincial support, the Cowan Recreation Centre will give families in one of Ontario's fastest-growing communities a place to be active and compete close to home. It will bring neighbours together and draw visitors to Kitchener, supporting local jobs and businesses and strengthening our community for years to come." - The Honourable Mike Harris, MPP for Kitchener–Conestoga

“Places like the Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park are where people of all ages build confidence, learn new skills and discover a lifelong passion for sport. Through the Community Sport and Recreation Infrastructure Fund, our government’s $10 million investment in the quad gymnasium gives athletes more space to train and compete, more room for families to stay active, and more opportunities for Kitchener to host the events and tournaments that bring visitors and economic activity to the region.” - Jess Dixon, MPP for Kitchener South–Hespeler and Parliamentary Assistant to the Minister of Sport.
ABOUT THE COWAN RECREATION CENTRE AT RBJ SCHLEGEL PARK
The Cowan Recreation Centre is among the largest and most sustainable municipally owned recreation centres in Canada.

The Centre offers diverse recreation opportunities with a quad gymnasium, FIFA-sized indoor turf field, cricket practice nets, competition and leisure pools, and an indoor walking track, supporting sports and activities ranging from basketball and soccer to pickleball, badminton and swimming.

Together, RBJ Schlegel Park and the Cowan Recreation Centre create one of Waterloo Region’s premier recreation destinations, bringing together outdoor sports fields, a cricket pitch, pickleball, tennis and basketball courts, playgrounds and a splashpad with year-round indoor amenities including aquatics, turf fields, indoor cricket nets, a quad gymnasium, walking track and community spaces, offering recreation, sport and connection for all ages in every season.

The facility is the most accessible building ever constructed by the City of Kitchener, designed to meet the City's highest accessibility standards and shaped through input from residents with lived experience. It features pool ramps, wider pathways, tactile wayfinding elements and accessible viewing areas.

title: Nominate long-standing local businesses for a City of Kitchener Business Heritage Award
content: Local businesses play a vital role in shaping Kitchener's economy, culture and community. To celebrate their lasting contributions, the City of Kitchener is now accepting nominations for the Business Heritage Awards.

The Business Heritage Awards recognize long-standing Kitchener businesses and not-for-profit organizations that were established and operate in Kitchener, and have reached milestone anniversaries of 25, 50, 75 or 100 years of service. Eligible organizations of all sizes and sectors, including retail, manufacturing, service-based, family-owned and not-for-profit organizations, are encouraged to participate.

Through this award, local businesses and entrepreneurs are celebrated and recognized for investing in Kitchener, creating jobs, and helping to build a resilient, vibrant community. Their lasting impact continues to shape Kitchener's future.
Residents are invited to nominate local businesses that have celebrated a milestone anniversary between January 1, 2023, and December 31, 2026.
Nominations will be accepted until March 1, 2027 , with award recipients to be recognized at an awards event in Spring 2027.
To nominate a business, visit Kitchener.ca/BusinessHeritageAwards.

title: Statement from Mayor Berry Vrbanovic on Remembrance Day
content: Today, residents in the City of Kitchener will gather with Canadians in communities large and small from coast to coast to coast to mark Remembrance Day and honour the brave women and men who served our country in times of war, military conflict and peacekeeping missions.

Remembrance Day is an opportunity to pause, reflect and pay tribute to all those who have answered the call to serve. We remember those who made the ultimate sacrifice, veterans who returned home carrying the lasting impacts of service, members of the Canadian Armed Forces, reservists and cadets who continue to serve today, and the families and loved ones who support them through that service. Together, they have helped defend the values and freedoms we hold dear.

Here in Kitchener, remembrance is reflected in the places and traditions we share. Whether at the Kitchener Memorial Auditorium, built as a lasting tribute to those whose service and sacrifice shaped our community, or at the Kitchener Cenotaph, we continue to honour the legacy of veterans and military families whose contributions have helped build the country and community we know today.

As we wear our poppies and gather in remembrance, we are reminded that the freedoms we enjoy today were secured through extraordinary courage, service and sacrifice. We also recognize our shared responsibility to keep these stories alive for future generations and to ensure that those who served are never forgotten.

On behalf of the City, my Council colleagues and our residents,  I encourage everyone to take a moment today at 11am to reflect, remember and express our gratitude. In doing so, we honour those who served and reaffirm our commitment to the values they fought to protect.
Lest we forget.

title: Know Before You Go: Free nine-day Grand Opening Celebration at Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park begins November 14
content: A major community vision is becoming a reality. From November 14 to 22, residents are invited to celebrate the grand opening of Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park, the result of years of planning and construction, collaboration among all levels of government, support from community organizations, and the dedication of thousands of people who helped create a welcoming new place for Kitchener to connect, compete and belong.

The free, nine-day grand opening celebration kicks off with an official ribbon cutting, taking place on the centre’s  fieldhouse from 10 to 11:30 a.m. Immediately following the ceremony, residents are invited to explore the facility and experience all it has to offer, with family activities, recreation experiences, facility tours, aquatics programming, sport showcases and more. With strong attendance expected, visitors are encouraged to plan ahead and prepare for a milestone celebration for the entire community.

Parking at RBJ Schlegel Park will be limited, particularly on opening weekend. Visitors are encouraged to plan their trip in advance and allow extra travel time throughout the celebration. The City encourages residents to:
Take Grand River Transit. To make it easier to get to the grand opening celebration, Route 33 will detour on November 14 to serve a temporary stop at Wallaceton Way. Plan your trip at grt.ca.
Carpool with friends, family or teammates.
Walk or cycle if travelling from nearby neighbourhoods.
Arrive early for registered programs and high-demand activities.
Check event schedules before leaving home.
November 14 | 10 a.m. to 11:30 a.m.

Join Mayor Berry Vrbanovic, members of Council and community partners including MP Tim Louis and MPPs Mike Harris, and Jess Dixon, and local sport partners, as the City officially opens the new facility and celebrates a new chapter for recreation, sport and community connection in Kitchener.
November 14 | Noon to 6 p.m.; Free registered programming: 7-10 p.m.

Enjoy family-friendly entertainment, inflatables, face painting, mascots, community displays, public swims and opportunities to explore the facility. Additional free registered programming will take place from 7 to 10 p.m.
November 15 to 20 | All day
Residents can experience free programming including:
Public swims
Fitness and wellness classes
Recreation sports
Active aging programs
Youth activities
Family activities and play all day drop-in programming
Facility tours
Most activities require advance registration beginning November 2.
November 21 and 22 | All day
Meet local sport organizations, watch demonstrations and learn about opportunities to get active in Kitchener's sport and recreation community.
To make the most of your visit:
Pre-register for activities and programs where required.
Bring comfortable clothing and footwear if participating in recreation activities.
Pack swimwear and towels for aquatics programs.
Bring a reusable water bottle to take advantage of water refill stations within the facility
Review the event schedule in advance and identify the activities you would like to attend.
Pack your patience: there may be times with larger crowds and wait times for popular activities.
Dress for the weather if participating in outdoor activities or walking between parking areas and the facility.

The grand opening marks the beginning of a new chapter for recreation in Kitchener. Residents are invited to join the celebration and discover how Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park is a place where people can connect, compete and belong.
For schedules, registration information and event details, visit Kitchener.ca/RBJSchlegelPark .

title: Remembrance Day ceremonies and City of Kitchener facility closures
content: The City of Kitchener invites residents to come together this Remembrance Day to reflect on the sacrifices made by Canadians who have served our country. As a community that deeply respects and values its veterans and service members, Kitchener proudly honours their service and sacrifice.

“Remembrance Day is an opportunity to pause, reflect and pay tribute to those who answered the call to serve,” said Mayor Berry Vrbanovic. “I encourage residents to wear their poppy with pride, join us at the ceremony and, if you have veterans in your family, bring them with you as we honour their service and keep their legacy alive. By gathering in remembrance, we reaffirm our gratitude to those who served and strengthen our shared responsibility to remember their sacrifices.”
Remembrance Day ceremony

The community's annual Remembrance Day ceremony will take place on Wednesday, Nov. 11, from 10:45 a.m. to noon at the Kitchener Cenotaph, located at the corner of Duke Street and Frederick Street. In advance of the ceremony, Royal Canadian Legion Branch 50 Kitchener will be conducting a parade down King Street from Ontario Street to the cenotaph. We are grateful for their support in hosting this day of remembrance.

The ceremony will honour Canadian veterans, active members of the Canadian Armed Forces and all those who have served our country. Residents are encouraged to arrive early, wear their poppy and take part in this important tradition of remembrance. Families, veterans and community members of all ages are welcome to attend and pay their respects. There will be reserved seating available for veterans at the ceremony.
Additional ceremonies and days of remembrance

In addition to Kitchener's Remembrance Day ceremony, residents are encouraged to take part in other local commemorative events that honour veterans and reflect the diverse traditions of remembrance observed throughout our community.

Earlier this month, the annual Sikh Remembrance Day ceremony was held at the gravesite of Private Buckam Singh, recognizing the contributions and sacrifices of Sikh Canadians who served in the First World War.
Saturday, November 8 marked National Indigenous Veterans Day, honouring the service of First Nations, Inuit and Métis veterans.
On Sunday, November 15 at 2:30 p.m., the annual German Remembrance Day ceremony will be held at Woodland Cemetery.
City facility hours
The following facilities are closed on November 11:
Kitchener City Hall Service Centre. Kitchener City Hall remains open but no in-person services will be available.
Rockway Centre
Kitchener Market
Kitchener Bylaw office
These facilities remain open:
All community centres except Rockway Centre are open for regular hours
All indoor pools are open for regular hours
The Aud opens at 3 p.m. for free skates and rentals
Sportsworld Arena is open for regular hours
Activa Sportsplex is open for regular hours
Lions Arena is open from 4 – 10 p.m.
Don McLaren Arena is open from 3 – 10 p.m.
Grand River Arena is open from 4 – 10 p.m.
Together, let us pause, reflect and pay tribute to the Canadians who have served our country with courage and dedication.
For more information: Corporate Communications and Marketing City of Kitchener Media@kitchener.ca

title: Waterloo region municipalities launch a new pilot program, inviting developers to collaborate on building for the future
content: Waterloo - As of November 5, 2026, developers and builders across Waterloo region are invited to participate in a new voluntary pilot program to explore ways to make their developments more energy-efficient, resilient, and sustainable.

Through WR Community Energy , Waterloo Region municipalities are working together to advance a harmonized approach to building for our changing environment. The High-Performance Development Standards (HPDS) Pilot Program is the next step in exploring how high-performance development practices can be applied to real-world projects.

The HPDS are a suggested set of standards for consideration in new development applications in the Cities of Cambridge, Kitchener, and Waterloo, and the Townships of North Dumfries, Wellesley, Wilmot, and Woolwich.

Through standard planning application processes, this Pilot Program gives developers an opportunity to put these practices into action, share what works, and help shape future approaches to development in Waterloo region. These practices can help reduce energy and water use and keep utility bills low, prepare buildings and communities for a changing climate, and make better use of resources.

The program was developed through extensive engagement with municipal staff, the development industry and the community, technical analysis, and a review of best practices. It is the next step in exploring how these practices can work in real-world projects.
The pilot will explore measures such as:

Participation in the Pilot Program is voluntary and open to interested developers and builders through the planning application process. Participants will be invited to submit a Statement of Interest, with projects selected that will ensure a mix of building types and locations across Waterloo region.
All participating projects will be recognized with additional Bronze, Silver, Gold, and Energy Innovator recognition awarded to builders and developers based on the number of HPDS targets achieved.
This is an opportunity for developers and builders to showcase leadership in high-performance development, share lessons from real-world projects, and help shape future development in the Region.
The Pilot Program creates a space to explore what works, recognize industry leadership, and advance more efficient, resilient, and sustainable communities.

title: Statement from Mayor Berry Vrbanovic on the 2026 Federal Budget: Masters of Our Destiny
content: Today’s federal budget recognizes the real pressures people are feeling across Canada and here in Kitchener. We see them in the cost of groceries and housing, in our workplaces and across our neighbourhoods. This moment calls for meaningful action.

We welcome the federal government’s focus on making life more affordable and building a stronger, more independent Canadian economy. The budget identifies Canada’s highly skilled workforce, research institutions and capacity for innovation as strengths that can help our country compete and prosper.

Kitchener is ready to contribute. At the heart of Canada’s innovation and technology corridor, our community brings together skilled workers, entrepreneurs, researchers and companies developing ideas and products for markets at home and around the world. Kitchener has an important role to play as Canada strengthens its economic independence, helps Canadian businesses scale and creates good jobs here at home.

Housing is central to a more affordable future. Today’s budget reflects a shared commitment to accelerating homebuilding and lowering costs, to make housing more accessible to everyone in our community.

Kitchener is ready to be a strong partner and we have a proven record of delivering. We have modernized approvals, invested municipal funding, made land available and supported housing providers. Together, these efforts have helped enable roughly 2,000 affordable homes across 40 projects, including more than 184 supportive homes, with more underway.

New federal support for municipal e-permitting and technology-enabled approvals is also encouraging. Kitchener’s experience shows that modern processes and responsible stewardship can deliver meaningful results and we are ready to share what we have learned.

We also applaud the federal government’s 10-year $29-billion commitment towards supportive housing and services for people and communities, which was also announced in today’s budget. We recognize the difference an investment of this scale can make and will require orders of governments and communities to work together to get it right.

We’re pleased to see new investment through the Build Communities Strong Fund. Here in Kitchener, this partnership is helping us grow with purpose and create welcoming places where residents can connect, stay active and take part in community life.

The new $1.5-billion investment in arenas and community recreation facilities is a welcome opportunity for growing communities like ours. Recreation is a core municipal service and an important part of a healthy, connected city. Arenas, pools, sports fields and community centres are where children learn new skills, neighbours get to know one another, older adults stay active and people of all ages and abilities find a sense of belonging.

Kitchener’s soon-to-open Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park reflects that approach. Supported through the Build Communities Strong Fund, it will be a welcoming hub where people can be active, spend time together and participate in community life.

As Kitchener grows, we will continue to advocate for sustained investment in the infrastructure, facilities and services residents depend on. These investments help us build complete neighbourhoods, support more housing and provide stability for the future.

Kitchener is ready to work with the Government of Canada to turn national priorities into local results. We will bring our experience in housing delivery, our culture of innovation and our strong community partnerships to that work, while keeping the focus on what matters to people here at home.
